tolerance_html:
mechloop/tolerance/process.py holds, per process, the standard deviations the tolerance verifier built its 3000 simulated machines with. The sheets hold the fabricator to +/-2 standard deviations of the same figures, so a batch of parts inside the drawing tolerance is the population that was simulated. A part AT the limit everywhere is worse than what was simulated: the limits are not a licence to sit on them.

printing_html:
• Printer assumed by the manufacture verifier: build volume (220.0, 220.0, 220.0), nozzle 0.4 mm, layer 0.2 (the verifier default: the design does not declare one) mm.
  • Orientation: pinned per part in the design (print_up), listed below; the STL is already turned so the bed face is on Z = 0.
  • Walls and infill: not declared by the design. The verifier's mass and time estimate used: estimate: 1.2 mm walls, 20% infill, 5 mm3/s, no support material counted.
  • The FEA load cases treat every printed part as solid, isotropic material. A part printed at 20 % infill is not the part that was analysed. For the parts with a load case (), print solid or accept that the factor of safety is unverified.
  • No threads in plastic, no heat-set inserts: every screw in a printed part runs into a steel nut (captive pockets and slots are in the models).
  • Printed clearance holes are drawn at ISO 273 medium + 0.2 mm FDM allowance (M2.5 3.1, M3 3.6, M4 4.7, M5 5.7, M6 6.8; +0.3 and a teardrop or flat top for a hole whose axis lies in the build plane): vertical holes print undersize. Starting values: print a coupon of M3 holes 3.4 to 3.8 in 0.1 mm steps on the printer that will make the parts, then set the allowance and the slicer's hole compensation (docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md). Bearing seats and insert pockets are drawn to their own figures.

parts.name: carriage_plate_left
parts.desc: Carriage plate (left): one of three identical flat 1.6 mm 6061 plates. Its top 20 mm is bolted to the 2020 square's outer face (two M5, T-nuts); its bottom carries the guide block z_carriage_left (four M3 x 5 into the block's own threads). The 30 mm web between them is a flexure: stiff along the wall, soft square to it (251 N/mm), so this block locates the carrier along the wall only and a rail that is not exactly parallel, or a carrier that has grown warm, bends the web instead of loading the block.

parts.name: carriage_plate_right
parts.desc: Carriage plate (right): one of three identical flat 1.6 mm 6061 plates. Its top 20 mm is bolted to the 2020 square's outer face (two M5, T-nuts); its bottom carries the guide block z_carriage_right (four M3 x 5 into the block's own threads). The 30 mm web between them is a flexure: stiff along the wall, soft square to it (251 N/mm), so this block locates the carrier along the wall only and a rail that is not exactly parallel, or a carrier that has grown warm, bends the web instead of loading the block.

parts.name: carriage_plate_rear
parts.desc: Carriage plate (rear): one of three identical flat 1.6 mm 6061 plates. Its top 20 mm is bolted to the 2020 square's outer face (two M5, T-nuts); its bottom carries the guide block z_carriage_rear (four M3 x 5 into the block's own threads). The 30 mm web between them is a flexure: stiff along the wall, soft square to it (251 N/mm), so this block locates the carrier along the wall only and a rail that is not exactly parallel, or a carrier that has grown warm, bends the web instead of loading the block.

parts.name: nut_plate
parts.desc: Laser-cut 6061 nut plate under the carrier's square. How the bed is lifted: the POM anti-backlash nut z_nut (supplied on the motor's screw; dimensions a STAND-IN) rides lead screw leadscrew. Its square flange is under this 9.525 mm plate, which is bolted under the 2020 square's member sq_rear (two M5 from below into T-nuts) and reaches 57.1 mm out to the screw; the nut's barrel hangs below. The carrier's weight rests on the flange, so when the screw turns the nut climbs it and lifts the plate, the square, the deck and the bed. The M2.5 pin screw nut_pin (through a 5 mm aluminium sleeve, fixed in a corner hole of the flange) sits in a radial slot in the plate: it stops the nut turning with the screw while letting it float 2.8 mm sideways. The nut is captive: the laser-cut keeper nut_keeper, bolted 0.1 mm under the flange on two M3 through-bolts and spacers, stops the plate lifting off it.

parts.name: nut_plate_fr
parts.desc: Laser-cut 6061 nut plate under the carrier's square. How the bed is lifted: the POM anti-backlash nut z_nut_fr (supplied on the motor's screw; dimensions a STAND-IN) rides lead screw leadscrew_fr. Its square flange is under this 9.525 mm plate, which is bolted under the 2020 square's member sq_right (two M5 from below into T-nuts) and reaches 9.1 mm out to the screw; the nut's barrel hangs below. The carrier's weight rests on the flange, so when the screw turns the nut climbs it and lifts the plate, the square, the deck and the bed. The M2.5 pin screw nut_pin_fr (through a 5 mm aluminium sleeve, fixed in a corner hole of the flange) sits in a radial slot in the plate: it stops the nut turning with the screw while letting it float 2.8 mm sideways. The nut is captive: the laser-cut keeper nut_keeper_fr, bolted 0.1 mm under the flange on two M3 through-bolts and spacers, stops the plate lifting off it.

parts.bom_basis: catalogue level 'partial': switch figures (body, operating position 6.8 +/-1.5 mm, overtravel 0.55 mm min, movement differential 0.5 mm max, operating force 0.78 N max) are OMRON's D2F data sheet. Buy the gold-contact low-current type (D2F-01L): a general-purpose D2F needs 100 mA at 5 V as its minimum load, a 3.3 V logic input with a pull-up draws far less; D2F-01 needs 1 mA. The 20 x 12.5 mm carrier board is generated, not a known bought module: its terminal row (0.9 mm below the body bottom, 2.62 mm through the board) is kept as drawn. OMRON's right-angled terminals (-A) would be 2.6 +/-0.2 mm below the body bottom and 1.5 mm through a 1.6 mm board: re-check the three terminal holes once the bought module is known

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Bed probe on a thin spring-steel sheet: sensing distance unverified
open_items.known: Every probe figure (z_offset 2.0 mm, range [1.2, 2.8], face window [0.662, 2.538] mm) assumes the sensor switches at 4.0 mm, the maker's figure for a 1 mm iron target. The target here is 220 x 220 mm textured PEI spring-steel print sheet, held on bed_magnet by magnetism alone: lift it off to remove prints., 0.4 mm (a catalogue part) on its magnetic base. Basis recorded by the report: OMRON E2B data sheet (vendor_docs/omron_E2B_datasheet_en.pdf): p.2 ordering, p.7 ratings (M12, double distance, shielded), p.15 dimensions (E2B-M12KS04-WP), p.20 surrounding metal (double distance, shielded, M12): 4 mm +/-10 % on the standard iron target.
open_items.check: COMMISSIONING.md step B1 with the real sensor, sheet and magnet BEFORE ordering anything else; pass window there

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Mains side: printed hoods only, one bonded extrusion, not certified
open_items.known: Open frame; the inlet's rear, the relay module and the supply terminals are under printed hoods (mains_cover_relay, mains_cover_relay_screw_0, mains_cover_relay_screw_0_washer, mains_cover_relay_screw_0_nwasher, mains_cover_relay_screw_0_nut, mains_cover_relay_screw_1, mains_cover_relay_screw_1_washer, mains_cover_relay_screw_1_nwasher, mains_cover_relay_screw_1_nut, mains_cover_psu, mains_cover_psu_screw_0, mains_cover_psu_screw_0_washer, mains_cover_psu_screw_0_nwasher, mains_cover_psu_screw_0_nut, mains_cover_psu_screw_1, mains_cover_psu_screw_1_washer, mains_cover_psu_screw_1_nwasher, mains_cover_psu_screw_1_nut, mains_cover_inlet, mains_cover_inlet_screw_0, mains_cover_inlet_screw_0_washer, mains_cover_inlet_screw_0_nwasher, mains_cover_inlet_screw_0_nut, mains_cover_inlet_screw_1, mains_cover_inlet_screw_1_washer, mains_cover_inlet_screw_1_nwasher, mains_cover_inlet_screw_1_nut) that are open where the wires enter: touch protection depends on fully insulated receptacles and the hoods being fitted. The model earths the supply and one extrusion; everything else relies on anodised joints. The supply has a 115 / 230 V selector that must be set by hand.
open_items.check: WIRING.md mains section; continuity test E1; a competent person signs off the mains side

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Bed plate flatness: the figure the limit is worked with is a receiving check
open_items.known: Limit (a), out of flat as installed <= 0.3 mm, is met with the owner's 0.13 mm for the plate as bought plus the computed sag. The maker's brochure in the repository gives 0.381 mm for 6.35 to 15.9 mm cast plate (whole plate); on that figure alone (a) is exceeded and no MIC-6 plate thinner than 19 mm would pass. McMaster's listing could not be read from here.
open_items.check: check the cut 232 mm plate on arrival with a straight edge and feelers: accept it at 0.13 mm or better, or ask SendCutSend for a flatter piece

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: The Z nuts' dimensions are a stand-in
open_items.known: The POM anti-backlash nuts that come on the 17E19S1684AB4-330RA screws are drawn from the maker's photographs (flange 23 x 23 x 6, barrel 12.7 x 26, holes on 16 mm, +/-1.5 mm): no drawing is published and the datasheet could not be fetched. The nut plates' screw hole, pin slot, keeper hole and keeper spacers follow those figures.
open_items.check: measure one nut before cutting the nut plates and keepers; correct leadscrew_nut_pom_ab4 and re-run verify

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Z screws at full length stand close to the frame
open_items.known: Used as sold (330 mm), the screws' tops are at 400 to 401 mm. The front two stand 1.5 mm inboard of the top side rails' inner faces and 2.5 mm outboard of the X beam's ends, free at the top; the rear one stands outside the back wall. Run-out or whip of more than about 1 mm at the top would let a front screw touch the top side rail.
open_items.check: check each screw's run-out at its tip on arrival (motor running slowly); run the bed through its whole travel by hand before first power

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)

open_items.known: Each 17E19S1684AB4-330RA carries the bed along its screw on its own bearings; the maker states no axial rating.
open_items.check: get the datasheet and an axial rating from StepperOnline before ordering three

open_items.title: 95 screw heads and nuts bear without a washer on a slot, thin aluminium or a circuit board
open_items.known: 68 on a slot or oversize hole; 18 on thin aluminium; 9 on a circuit board. The design draws washers elsewhere; these are the ones left bare (captive nuts in laser-cut hex pockets, heads in the cast brackets' own slots, nuts on boards, heads on bought parts). Full list below.
open_items.check: decide per joint before assembly

open_items.title: Hand-assembled holes in laser-cut and printed parts have no lead-in (11 features)
open_items.known: A laser cut is square through the plate: no chamfer can be drawn. Bearing seats are three flats or clearance holes, the bought parts carry their own edge radii; the builder breaks the cut edges by hand. List below.
open_items.check: deburr each listed hole with a countersink tool before fitting

open_items.title: Sharp edges: the model has almost no fillets and no chamfers
open_items.known: Every laser-cut and machined part is drawn with sharp edges and corners. The drawings carry the note 'Deburr; break all sharp edges 0.2-0.5 mm; outside profile corners R1 min unless dimensioned', which is NOT yet in the CAD. The Y belts pass through laser-cut slots in 3 mm steel: a burr there cuts the belt.
open_items.check: deburr everything; stone the belt slots

open_items.title: Not in the design at all
open_items.known: Washers; Filament for the printed parts (masses per part in FABRICATION; Mains lead (IEC C13) for your country; the inlet's fuse drawer if the inlet is ordered without one (see the inlet line); microSD cards (control board flashing, host), a pin header for the host board if it comes without one; Accelerometer board for input-shaper measurement (commissioning step; e; Dial indicator with a stand, feeler gauges, a 1 kg mass, a straight edge and a square (commissioning and alignment); Thread-locking compound for pulley set screws and the bed posts' jam nuts; grease for the rails and lead screws; Filament path; Feet or pads under the frame; Covers for the mains terminals (relay module, inlet tabs, supply terminal block); Adhesive / cleaning materials for bonding the heater pad, thermal cut-off and magnetic sheet to the plate; high-temperature tape for the cut-off; Crimp tools for JST-XH, Micro-Fit, ferrules and quick-connects
open_items.check: BOM.md, last section

open_items.title: Changing the closed Z belt means lifting the bed carrier off all three lead screws
open_items.known: The loop runs round the three screws below the carrier; nothing in the design lets it be opened.
